Tom Buhler, director of business development for Butter Buds

State and local tax breaks could lure Butter Buds Food Ingredients into buying a 76,000-square-foot building and expanding in Racine instead of moving to Illinois.

The company, which produces food flavorings for retail and commercial use, has grown to 55 employees and plans to add 22 more in the next three years, said Tom Buhler, director of business development. But Butter Buds has outgrown its Racine facility, prompting the company's owner, Cumberland Packing Corp., New York City, to consider sites in the Chicago area, he said.

"If we located in Illinois, we would reduce our freight cost by 15 percent," Buhler said.

The threat of losing Butter Buds spurred the city of Racine and Wisconsin Economic Development Corp. to consider tax breaks to offset the company’s cost of staying in Racine. The city will rebate to Butter Buds 75 percent of its annual city property tax payments for 10 years, said Brian O'Connell, Racine director of development. As part of the agreement, the company has agreed to interview and potentially hire Racine residents to fill new jobs at Butter Buds, he said.

Buhler said the company has asked the state for tax breaks for every new job Butter Buds creates. The state offers tax breaks of up to $3,000 to $5,000 a year for new job creation. The Wisconsin Economic Development Corp. is reviewing the request, he said.

The company's plan to expand in Racine is contingent on the city and state approving the tax breaks, Buhler said.

"They’re focused on jobs," Buhler said of the government agencies. "First of all it's retaining 55 jobs that we have here and it's adding 22 jobs."

Butter Buds plans to buy a 5-acre site with a 76,000-square-foot industrial building that is immediately north of the company’s current home in the Olsen Industrial Park. The company would build a small addition to connect the two facilities. Buhler said he wants to buy the building and gain approval for the tax breaks by the end of July and move into the new facility by September.
